metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness supports a mid-turn SIGKILL. A committed same-agent recording proves that irrlichd records process_exited for the bound session and removes the row without an error transition.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario requires one real DeepSeek Harness session to enter `working`, lose its process before any durable `turn/end`, emit `process_exited`, and disappear without entering `error`. A SIGKILL is an operating-system action, so it does not depend on a DeepSeek Harness command. DeepSeek Harness writes `turn/start` before model completion, and the existing interactive driver can kill the live tmux pane process while that turn remains open.

The daemon result is settled by direct same-agent evidence, not only by parser inspection. The committed `session-end` recording runs this exact shape as variant 3. Its `events.jsonl` records the real session-UUID row as `ready` at seq 823, `working` at seq 827, PID 4796 at seq 846, and `process_exited` at seq 860. No later `ready`, `waiting`, or `error` transition occurs, and `transcript_removed` follows at seq 861. The archived transcript contains the third `turn/start` and no third `turn/end`. The manifest reports 14/14 phases passed on daemon 0.6.4+dff7bcc. `git diff dff7bcc82..HEAD` is empty for the DSH adapter, PID manager, process-exit tests, driver, and teardown helper.

The transport matches that evidence. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/dsh/parser.go` maps durable `turn/start` to working and only `turn/end` to turn completion. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/dsh/pid.go` binds the real session through its sibling `session.lock`. `PIDManager.HandleWatcherExit` fans a watcher edge to every row bound to the PID, and `HandleProcessExit` records `process_exited` and deletes the row in every state, including `working`. The regression tests pin both deletion and exactly one exit event for a mid-turn death.

The driver declares and implements every recipe primitive. Its `sigkill` step kills the stored pane PID and uses the shared bounded death poll. The recipe copies both committed scenario-sibling timings: six seconds before SIGKILL and twenty seconds after it. It uses a 1000-token repeated-token prompt so the local model remains active through the kill window. The spec selects a real `session-` UUID, pins PID discovery and exit to that row, and rejects any durable `turn/end` or transition to ready, waiting, or error before exit.
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: without the session-UUID selector, same-session pins, and the zero-turn/end assertion, a proc-<PID> pre-session or an already-completed idle turn could satisfy the exit phase while proving no mid-turn crash. The spec includes all three guards.

The prompt length and six-second pre-kill delay are load-bearing environment inputs. Re-probe LM Studio at record time and confirm that qwen/qwen3.5-9b is still serving and that the 1000-token response has not written turn/end before SIGKILL. The spec must fail if the model completes early.

Metric observations are omitted because SIGKILL can occur before an assistant usage record becomes durable. This cell asserts lifecycle and process-exit behavior. A token or model assertion would make the result depend on how much generation was flushed before the kill.
This cell duplicates the mid-turn SIGKILL variant in DeepSeek Harness session-end. Its separate value is a named regression lock for the removed crash inference described by scenario 2.25.

sources.note: Direct same-agent evidence: seq 823 ready, seq 827 working, seq 846 PID binding, seq 860 process_exited, and seq 861 transcript_removed for the third real session. No ready, waiting, or error transition follows turn start.
Reports DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2, daemon 0.6.4+dff7bcc, and 14/14 passing phases for the three teardown variants.
The concatenated three-session archive contains three turn/start records but only two turn/end records. The SIGKILL variant is the final session, so its durable turn remains open.
Maps turn/start to working and turn/end to turn_done; a transcript frozen after turn/start therefore remains working until process exit.
Declares the compressed FilesUnderRoot source, process matcher, and lock-based PID discovery for DeepSeek Harness.
Discovers the live session PID from the writer of the sibling session.lock file.
HandleWatcherExit fans an exit edge to all PID holders. HandleProcessExit records process_exited and deletes the session regardless of state, including mid-turn working.
TestHandleProcessExit_MidTurnExitDeletesTheRow and TestHandleProcessExit_RecordsProcessExitedForAMidTurnDeath pin the required deletion and event behavior.
Declares and implements send, sleep, and sigkill. The sigkill step targets the stored pane PID and waits for death through the shared teardown helper.
Provides the committed six-second pre-kill and twenty-second post-kill scenario timing. Muse uses the same timing.

preconditions: dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 or newer is on PATH and the community tui profile is installed under the active DSH home
LM Studio is serving qwen/qwen3.5-9b through http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1
irrlichd is recording with DeepSeek Harness transcript permission granted
the local model remains slow enough that the 1000-token response is still open six seconds after turn/start; verify this from turn/end absence, not from timing alone
setup: Let the driver create one fresh cwd and one fresh DSH session under the recording staging directory
Let the driver apply the LM Studio endpoint and model through its per-run temporary patch
recipe.scope_note: Matches both committed scenario siblings: six seconds before sigkill and twenty seconds after sigkill. The repeated-token prompt is longer than the existing DSH session-end variant so the model remains inside the turn across the longer sibling delay.

script.text: Output the token COFFEE separated by one space exactly 1000 times. Do not use tools and do not add other text.

verify: events.jsonl contains one real session-UUID row that enters working and binds a PID
the same real session emits process_exited after SIGKILL and then disappears
no ready, waiting, or error transition occurs between turn start and process exit
the DSH transcript contains turn/start and no turn/end
the transcript contains no tool/call record
